questions.prompt: When did you first use the internet?
questions.sampleA1: I... internet... when I was... small. I play games.
questions.sampleA2: I first used the internet when I was a child. I think I was maybe eight years old. We had a computer at home and I used it to play games and look at pictures. It was fun, but it was very slow.
questions.sampleB1: I think I first used the internet when I was around ten years old. We had dial-up, which was incredibly slow compared to today. I mainly used it for school projects, like researching animals, and also to play online games. It was pretty basic back then, but I remember being really excited about it. However, it was also very annoying when the phone line was busy.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I first got online when I was about nine or ten, back in the early two-thousands. We had a clunky desktop with a dial-up connection that took ages to load anything. I mostly used it to look up things for school and mess around with a few simple games. Looking back, it honestly feels like a completely different world.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men... internet... men... kichkina bo'lganimda. Men o'yinlar o'ynayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men birinchi marta internetdan bolaligimda foydalanganman. O'ylashimcha, men sakkiz yoshda bo'lganman. Uyda kompyuterimiz bor edi va men undan o'yin o'ynash va rasmlarga qarash uchun foydalanardim. Bu qiziqarli edi, lekin juda sekin edi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, internetdan birinchi marta o'n yoshlarimda foydalanganman. Bizda dial-up aloqasi bor edi, u bugungi kunga nisbatan juda sekin edi. Men asosan undan maktab loyihalari uchun, masalan, hayvonlarni o'rganish uchun va onlayn o'yinlar o'ynash uchun foydalandim. O'sha paytda u juda oddiy edi, lekin men bundan juda xursand bo'lganimni eslayman.
Shunga qaramay, telefon liniyasi band bo'lganda ham juda asabiylashardim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men internetga birinchi marta to'qsoninchi yillarning oxirida, taxminan to'qqiz yoki o'n yoshlarimda duch kelganimni eslayman. Bizda dial-up modemli katta stol kompyuterimiz bor edi va ulanish jarayoni har doim sabr-toqatni talab qilardi. Dastlab, mening foydalanishim maktab topshiriqlari uchun ma'lumot qidirish va oddiy onlayn o'yinlar o'ynash bilan cheklangan edi. O'sha davrdagi internet bugungi standartlarga ko'ra ibtidoiy bo'lsa-da, u raqamli aloqa va ma'lumot olish imkoniyatlariga bo'lgan qiziqishimni albatta uyg'otdi. O'ylaymanki, bu keyinchalik hayotimda texnologiyaga bo'lgan qiziqishimni shakllantirdi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - When did you first use the internet?
idioms: in its infancy - "go'daklik (boshlang'ich) davrida"
a far cry from - "...dan butunlay farq qiluvchi (hozirgi vaqt bilan solishtirganda)"
the early days - "ilk kunlar / boshlang'ich paytlar"
phrases: dial-up modem - "telefon tarmog'i orqali internetga ulanuvchi modem"
sentenceStarters: "I first used the internet when I was in primary school, probably…" - "Men internetdan birinchi marta boshlang'ich sinfda o'qiyotganimda foydalanganman, ehtimol…"
"Initially, I only used it to play simple flash games or…" - "Dastlab, men undan faqat oddiy flesh o'yinlar o'ynash yoki … uchun foydalanganman."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I first used the internet when I was in primary school, probably around the age of eight. Back then, connection speeds were agonizingly slow, and we had to rely on a dial-up modem that made a terrible screeching noise.
Initially, I only used it to play simple flash games or search for basic information for school projects. It is truly mind-boggling to see how exponentially the digital landscape has evolved since those "early days."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men internetdan birinchi marta boshlang'ich maktabda o'qiganimda foydalanganman, taxminan sakkiz yoshimda bo'lganman. O'sha paytlarda ulanish tezligi juda sekin edi va biz dahshatli g'ichirlagan ovoz chiqaradigan dial-up modemga tayanishimiz kerak edi.

Dastlab, men undan faqat oddiy flesh o'yinlarini o'ynash yoki maktab loyihalari uchun asosiy ma'lumotlarni qidirish uchun foydalanardim. O'sha "dastlabki kunlardan" beri raqamli landshaft qanchalik tez rivojlanganini ko'rish haqiqatan ham hayratlanarli.

questions.prompt: Do you pay attention to your diet?
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I pay attention. I eat fruit and vegetables. But I also eat chocolate sometimes because it is good.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I try to pay attention to my diet. I think it's important for my health. I try to eat healthy food like vegetables and fruit. However, sometimes I eat fast food because it's easy.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I'd say I'm fairly health-conscious, to be honest. I try to cut down on sugar and processed stuff, and I load up on vegetables and fruit whenever I can. That said, I'm no saint — I do give in to the odd slice of cake. I suppose it's all about striking a healthy balance rather than being too strict.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men ovqat yeyman. Menga pizza yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men e'tibor beraman. Men meva va sabzavotlar yeyman. Lekin men ba'zida shokolad ham yeyman, chunki u mazali.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men ovqatlanishimga e'tibor berishga harakat qilaman. Menimcha, bu sog'lig'im uchun muhim. Sabzavotlar va mevalar kabi sog'lom ovqatlarni yeyishga harakat qilaman.
Shunga qaramay, ba'zida tez tayyorlanadigan ovqatlarni yeyman, chunki bu oson.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men, odatda, ovqatlanishimga e'tibor beraman, deb ayta olaman, garchi har doim ham mukammal emasman. Ko'pincha sog'lom tanlovlar qilishga harakat qilaman, yangi masalliqlar va muvozanatli ovqatlarga e'tibor qarataman. Yaxshi ovqatlanish jismoniy va ruhiy farovonlik uchun juda muhim ekanligini bilaman. Albatta, ba'zida unchalik sog'lom bo'lmagan narsalarni iste'mol qilishim mumkin, lekin men buni doimiy odatdan ko'ra ko'proq xursandchilik deb bilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you pay attention to your diet?
idioms: you are what you eat - "nimani yesangiz o'sha sizsiz (ovqatlanish tananing holatini belgilaydi)"
watch one's weight - "vazniga e'tibor bermoq (kuzatmoq)"
eat like a bird - "qushdek (juda kam) ovqat yemoq"
phrases: guilty pleasure - "zavq beruvchi, ammo zararli ekanini bilib qilingan ish / yegulik"
sentenceStarters: "I try to be highly conscious of my diet by avoiding…" - "Men … dan voz kechish orqali ratsionimga nisbatan juda e'tiborli bo'lishga harakat qilaman."
"Occasionally, I might indulge in a guilty pleasure like…" - "Vaqti-vaqti bilan men … kabi zararliroq yeguliklarga o'zimga ruxsat beraman."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely. I try to be highly conscious of my diet by avoiding overly processed foods and reducing my sugar intake. I firmly believe that maintaining a balanced diet is essential for long-term health.
Occasionally, I might indulge in a guilty pleasure like a slice of chocolate cake, but I generally stick to wholesome, nutritious meals because I subscribe to the belief that "you are what you eat."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta. Men haddan tashqari qayta ishlangan mahsulotlardan qochish va shakar iste'molini kamaytirish orqali ovqatlanishimga juda e'tibor berishga harakat qilaman. Men uzoq muddatli salomatlik uchun muvozanatli ovqatlanish muhim, deb qat'iy ishonaman.

Vaqti-vaqti bilan shokoladli tort bo'lagi kabi "gunohkor lazzat"dan bahramand bo'lishim mumkin, lekin men odatda foydali, to'yimli ovqatlarga amal qilaman, chunki men "nima yesang, shusan" degan fikrga qo'shilaman.

questions.prompt: Do many people in your country using bicycles?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I have bike. My friend have bike.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, some people use bikes. I see bikes in the park and on the street. It is good for exercise, and it is cheap.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I think a lot of people in my country use bicycles. Especially in the cities, because it's easier than driving. Also, it's good for your health. However, it's not so common in the countryside.
questions.sampleB2: Well, it's definitely catching on, especially in the bigger cities. A lot of people are taking up cycling either to keep fit or to get around without getting stuck in traffic. The thing is, the government has started building proper bike lanes, which makes it far safer. In the countryside, though, cars are still the norm, so it's a real mixed picture.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menda velosiped bor. Mening do'stimda velosiped bor.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, ba'zi odamlar velosipedlardan foydalanadi. Men velosipedlarni parkda va ko'chada ko'raman. Bu jismoniy mashqlar uchun yaxshi va arzon.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menimcha, mening mamlakatimda ko'p odamlar velosipedlardan foydalanadi.
Ayniqsa, shaharlarda, chunki bu mashina haydashdan osonroq.
Bundan tashqari, bu sizning sog'lig'ingiz uchun foydali.
Biroq, qishloq joylarda bu unchalik keng tarqalgan emas.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, mening mamlakatimda velosipedlarning ommaviyligi albatta o'sib bormoqda. Ayniqsa, shahar joylarida velosipedda yurgan odamlarni tobora ko'proq ko'ryapsiz. Menimcha, buning sababi qisman atrof-muhit muammolari haqida xabardorlikning oshishi va sog'lom turmush tarziga intilishdir. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi shaharlar velosiped infratuzilmasini yaxshilashga sarmoya kiritmoqda, bu esa ko'proq odamlarni qisqa masofalarga mashinalar o'rniga velosipedlarni tanlashga undaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do many people in your country using bicycles?
idioms: kill two birds with one stone - "bir o'q bilan ikki quyonni urmoq"
jump on the bandwagon - "ommabop(trenddagi) narsaga qo'shilmoq (masalan velosiped haydash modasi)"
pedal to the metal - "bor kuch bilan tezlashmoq (garchi ko'proq mashinaga xos bo'lsa ham)"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, cycling has become increasingly popular in recent years, especially in…" - "Ha, velosiped haydash so'nggi yillarda, ayniqsa … larda tobora ommalashib bormoqda."
"Moreover, the government has actively invested in building…" - "Bundan tashqari, hukumat … qurishga faol sarmoya kiritdi."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, cycling has become increasingly popular in recent years, especially in major cities. Many locals use bicycles for their daily commute because it is an eco-friendly alternative to driving and helps them avoid traffic congestion.
Moreover, the government has actively invested in building dedicated bike lanes, making it much safer. People are realizing that cycling kills two birds with one stone—it improves cardiovascular health while simultaneously protecting the environment.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, so'nggi yillarda velosiped haydash tobora ommalashib bormoqda, ayniqsa yirik shaharlarda. Ko'plab mahalliy aholi velosipedlardan kundalik ishga borish uchun foydalanadi, chunki bu mashina haydashga ekologik toza alternativa va ularga tirbandlikdan qochishga yordam beradi.

Bundan tashqari, hukumat maxsus velosiped yo'laklarini qurishga faol sarmoya kiritmoqda, bu esa uni ancha xavfsizroq qiladi. Odamlar velosiped haydash bir o'q bilan ikki quyonni urishini anglashmoqda - u bir vaqtning o'zida yurak-qon tomir salomatligini yaxshilaydi va atrof-muhitni himoya qiladi.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
Picture one, family. Happy.

Picture two, one person. Watching TV.
questions.sampleA2:
I see a family. They are watching TV and they are happy.

And I see one person. He is watching TV too, but he is alone.

Maybe he is sad.
questions.sampleB1:
In the first picture, I see a family watching a movie together. They look like they are having a good time.

The second picture shows a person who is watching a movie by himself. Maybe he prefers to watch alone.

I think both are okay, but I prefer watching with friends.
questions.sampleB2: So in the first picture, I can see a whole family — mum, dad and two kids — curled up on the sofa together, watching a fantasy film on a big wall-mounted TV. The dad has his arm around them and the mood looks really warm. In the second one, by contrast, there's a young woman on her own, wrapped in a blanket with earphones in and a cat asleep on her lap, watching a drama on her laptop. The key difference, I suppose, is that one is a shared, social experience while the other is quiet and solitary.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Birinchi rasm, oila. Baxtli.

Ikkinchi rasm, bir kishi. Televizor ko'ryapti.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men bir oilani ko'ryapman. Ular televizor ko'rishyapti va ular xursand.

Va men bir odamni ko'ryapman. U ham televizor ko'ryapti, lekin u yolg'iz.

Balki u qayg'ulidir.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda men bir oilani birgalikda kino ko'rayotganini ko'ryapman. Ularning kayfiyatlari yaxshi ko'rinadi.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa yolg'iz o'zi kino ko'rayotgan odamni ko'rsatadi. Ehtimol, u yolg'iz ko'rishni afzal ko'radi.

Menimcha, ikkalasi ham yaxshi, lekin men do'stlarim bilan ko'rishni afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda bir oila birgalikda kino kechasidan zavqlanayotganini ko'rish mumkin. Bu juda ham iliq va yaqinlashtiruvchi tajriba ekanligi ko'rinib turibdi, hamma bir lahzani baham ko'rmoqda.

Bunga zid ravishda, ikkinchi rasmda kimdir noutbukda yolg'iz kino tomosha qilayotgani ko'rsatilgan. Bu ko'ngilochar vaqtni o'tkazishning ancha yakka shaklini taklif qiladi.

Ikkala rasm ham film tomosha qilishni o'z ichiga olgan bo'lsa-da, ular odamlarning bo'sh vaqtlarini o'tkazishning turli usullarini ta'kidlaydi, biri jamoaviy, ikkinchisi esa individualistik.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe the pictures
idioms: in stark contrast - "keskin farq qilgan holda"
a lone wolf - "yolg'iz bo'ri (yolg'izlikni xush ko'ruvchi shaxs)"
quality time - "mazmunli o'tkazilgan vaqt"
phrases: introspective activity - "o'z xayollari bilan band(chuqur fikrga cho'mgan) mashg'ulot"
sentenceStarters: "The first picture shows a family huddled together on a sofa, joyfully…" - "Birinchi rasmda divanda to'planib, quvonch bilan … yotgan oila ko'rsatilgan."
"In stark contrast, the second picture displays an individual…" - "Bunga ziddiyat o'laroq, ikkinchi rasmda o'zicha yolg'iz… inson tasvirlangan."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The first picture shows a family huddled together on a sofa, joyfully watching a movie. The atmosphere is incredibly warm and convivial, highlighting a classic bonding experience where everyone is interacting and sharing laughter.
In stark contrast, the second picture displays an individual sitting quietly by themselves, watching a film on a laptop. This setting clearly represents a solitary, introspective activity. While the first image focuses on shared entertainment, the second beautifully illustrates the modern desire for personalized, uninterrupted escapism.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda bir oila divanda birga o'tirib, xursandchilik bilan kino tomosha qilayotganini ko'rish mumkin. Atmosfera juda iliq va samimiy, bu har bir kishi o'zaro muloqotda bo'lib, kulgini baham ko'radigan klassik birlashuv tajribasini ta'kidlaydi.

Bunga keskin zid o'laroq, ikkinchi rasmda bir shaxs yolg'iz o'zi kompyuterda film tomosha qilib o'tirgani aks etgan. Bu holat aniq yolg'izlikni, ichki o'y-fikrlarga berilish faoliyatini ifodalaydi. Birinchi rasm umumiy ko'ngil ochishga qaratilgan bo'lsa, ikkinchisi shaxsiy, uzluksiz hordiq chiqarishga bo'lgan zamonaviy istakni chiroyli tarzda tasvirlaydi.

questions.prompt: How can watching movies together strengthen family relationships?
questions.sampleA1: I like movies. My family watches movies. It is fun.
questions.sampleA2: I like to watch movies with my family. We eat popcorn and it's good. I think it's nice because we are together and we laugh.
questions.sampleB1: I think watching movies together is good for families. It's a way to spend time together, and you can talk about the movie afterwards. For example, we watched a funny movie last week and we all laughed a lot. Also, it's just relaxing to sit together and watch something interesting.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I think it really brings everyone together. In our busy lives, sitting down for a film is often the one time the whole family is in the same room. On top of that, it gives you something to chat about afterwards — you can bond over the story or the characters. To be honest, those shared laughs are exactly what create lasting memories.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men kinolarni yaxshi ko'raman. Mening oilam kinolar ko'radi. Bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men oilam bilan birga kino ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Biz popkorn yeymiz va bu yaxshi. Menimcha, bu yaxshi, chunki biz birgamiz va kulamiz.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, filmlarni birga tomosha qilish oilalar uchun yaxshi. Bu birga vaqt o'tkazishning bir usuli va keyin film haqida gaplashishingiz mumkin.
Masalan, o'tgan hafta biz kulgili film tomosha qildik va hammamiz juda ko'p kuldik. Bundan tashqari, birga o'tirib, qiziqarli narsani tomosha qilish shunchaki dam olishga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Filmlarni birgalikda tomosha qilish oilaviy munosabatlarni albatta yaxshilashi mumkin. Bu o'zaro ta'sirni rag'batlantiradigan va birlik tuyg'usini yaratadigan umumiy faoliyatni taklif etadi. Tomosha qilgandan so'ng, film mavzular, personajlar yoki hatto shaxsiy tajribalar haqida suhbatlar uchun boshlang'ich nuqta bo'lishi mumkin. Bu oila a'zolariga bir-birini yaxshiroq tushunishga yordam beradi.
Bundan tashqari, bu uzoq muddatli aloqalarni o'rnatish uchun muhim bo'lgan umumiy bo'sh vaqt an'anasini yaratadi. Bu band dunyoda bog'lanishning nisbatan oddiy usuli.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Watching movies together
idioms: the family that plays together, stays together - "birga o'ynaydigan (hordiq chiqaradigan) oila birga qoladi"
break the ice - "muzni yormoq (ortiqcha rasmiyatchilik yoki tushunmovchilikni yo'qotmoq)"
on the same wavelength - "bir xil to'lqinda (fikri bir joydan chiqmoq)"
phrases: quality time - "e'tibor va mehr bilan o'tkazilgan qimmatli vaqt"
sentenceStarters: "Watching movies as a group acts as a remarkably powerful catalyst for…" - "Guruh bo'lib kino ko'rish … uchun mutlaqo kuchli turtki(katalizator) bo'lib xizmat qiladi."

"Secondly, a thought-provoking film can serve as an excellent icebreaker, allowing…" - "Ikkinchidan, o'ylanishga chorlaydigan film juda zo'r 'muzni yoruvchi' vazifasini o'tab, … ga imkon berishi mumkin."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Watching movies as a group acts as a remarkably powerful catalyst for family bonding. Firstly, it provides a shared experience. In today's fast-paced world, sitting down together guarantees dedicated quality time free from the distractions of separate devices.
Secondly, it naturally sparks meaningful conversations. A thought-provoking film can serve as an excellent icebreaker, allowing parents and children to discuss complex moral dilemmas, emotions, and life lessons comfortably in a safe environment.
Ultimately, creating these cozy traditions builds long-lasting memories. Laughing at a comedy or anticipating a thriller's climax ensures that the family remains emotionally connected, proving that "the family that plays together, stays together."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birgalikda kino tomosha qilish oilaviy rishtalarni mustahkamlash uchun juda kuchli katalizator vazifasini o'taydi. Birinchidan, bu umumiy tajriba taqdim etadi. Bugungi tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda birga o'tirish alohida qurilmalarning chalg'ituvchi omillaridan xoli bo'lgan sifatli vaqtni kafolatlaydi.

Ikkinchidan, bu tabiiy ravishda mazmunli suhbatlarni keltirib chiqaradi. Fikrga soluvchi film ota-onalar va bolalarga murakkab axloqiy dilemmalar, his-tuyg'ular va hayot saboqlarini xavfsiz muhitda qulay tarzda muhokama qilish imkonini beruvchi ajoyib muz yorar vazifasini o'tashi mumkin.

Va nihoyat, bunday qulay an'analarni yaratish uzoq muddatli xotiralarni shakllantiradi. Komediyaga kulish yoki trillerning kulminatsion nuqtasini kutish oilaning hissiy jihatdan bog'langanligini ta'minlaydi va "birga o'ynaydigan oila birga qoladi" degan maqolni isbotlaydi.

questions.prompt: Why do some individuals enjoy watching films on their own?
questions.sampleA1: I like watch movie. I alone. Is good.
questions.sampleA2: I like to watch films. I like alone because I can stop it when I want. And I can eat my popcorn.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some people like watching films alone because they can relax. For example, they can pause the film to go to the toilet. Also, they don't have to talk to anyone. It can be more comfortable, I think.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose the main appeal is total freedom. When you're on your own, you can pause whenever you like, skip through the boring bits, and nobody's chatting away next to you. The thing is, it's also a great way to switch off and unwind after a long day. Plus, you don't have to compromise on what genre to watch.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men kino ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men yolg'izman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men filmlar ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men yolg'iz ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki xohlaganimda to'xtata olaman. Va men o'z popkornimni yeyishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar filmlarni yolg'iz tomosha qilishni yoqtirishadi, chunki ular dam olishlari mumkin.
Masalan, ular hojatxonaga borish uchun filmni to'xtatib qo'yishlari mumkin.
Shuningdek, ular hech kim bilan gaplashishlari shart emas.
Menimcha, bu qulayroq bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ba'zi odamlar filmlarni yolg'iz tomosha qilishdan zavqlanishadi, chunki bu ularga ko'proq diqqatni jamlash va shaxsiy tajribaga ega bo'lish imkonini beradi. Ular hech qanday chalg'ituvchi omillarsiz hikoyaga to'liq sho'ng'ishlari mumkin.
Qolaversa, ular film haqida boshqa hech kimning xohishlari yoki fikrlari bilan hisoblashishlari shart emas. Bu dam olish va filmdan butunlay o'z shartlari asosida zavqlanish usuli. Bundan tashqari, bu nima tomosha qilish haqida bahslashmaslikning ham bir usuli bo'lishi mumkin!

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Watching films on their own
idioms: me-time - "o'zim uchun vaqt"
what the doctor ordered - "ayni muddao (shifokor buyurgandek)"
get lost in something - "biror narsaga(kino) qattiq berilib ketmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Many people greatly prefer the solitude of watching films alone because…" - "Ko'pchilik odamlar filmlarni yolg'iz ko'rishni xush ko'radilar, chunki…"
"Furthermore, solitary viewing acts as an exceptional form of…" - "Bundan tashqari, yolg'iz boshga tomosha qilish … ning ajoyib shakli bo'lib xizmat qiladi."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many people greatly prefer the solitude of watching films alone because it offers unprecedented control over their entertainment. They can pause the movie whenever they want, rewind confusing dialogue, and completely immerse themselves without annoying interruptions from chatter.
Furthermore, solitary viewing acts as an exceptional form of escapism. After a long, stressful day of interacting with others, disappearing into a fictional universe allows them to mentally recharge their batteries entirely on their own terms.
Lastly, movie tastes are highly subjective. Watching alone means you don't have to compromise on genre, avoiding the tedious process of finding a film that satisfies everyone in a group. Sometimes, a little "me-time" is exactly what the doctor ordered.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilik odamlar filmlarni yolg'iz tomosha qilishni juda afzal ko'rishadi, chunki bu ularga o'z ko'ngilochar vaqtlarini misli ko'rilmagan darajada nazorat qilish imkoniyatini beradi. Ular filmni xohlagan vaqtda to'xtatib, tushunarsiz dialoglarni orqaga qaytarib, suhbatlardan kelib chiqadigan bezovta qiluvchi xalaqitlarsiz o'zlarini butunlay his qilishlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, yolg'iz tomosha qilish ajoyib bir qochish shakli sifatida xizmat qiladi. Boshqalar bilan uzoq, stressli kun davomida muloqot qilgandan so'ng, fantastik olamga g'oyib bo'lish ularga o'z shartlariga ko'ra, aqliy jihatdan batareykalarini to'liq quvvatlantirishga imkon beradi.

Nihoyat, kino didlari juda sub'ektivdir. Yolg'iz tomosha qilish siz janr bo'yicha murosaga kelishingizga hojat yo'q degani, bu guruhdagi hamma uchun maqbul bo'lgan filmni topishning zerikarli jarayonidan qochish demakdir. Ba'zan, ozgina "o'zim uchun vaqt" aynan shifokor buyurgan narsadir.

questions.prompt: Can you describe a place where people often meet friends?
questions.sampleA1: Park. I go park. See friends. Play.
questions.sampleA2: I like to meet my friends at the cafe. It's near my house and it has good coffee. We talk and laugh there. It's nice.
questions.sampleB1: I usually meet my friends at a local coffee shop. It's a comfortable place with good music, and we can sit and talk for hours. I think it's popular because it's easy to get to and the atmosphere is very relaxed. Also, they have really good cake!
questions.sampleB2: Right, so a place where people in my city often meet up with friends is the local coffee shop on the main square. It's a really cosy little spot, with comfy armchairs, warm lighting and, honestly, the best cakes in town. The great thing about it is that it's right in the centre, so it's a stone's throw away from wherever you happen to be. People go there to catch up over a coffee, chat for hours, or just hang out after work. You'll often see students revising, colleagues on their lunch break, or old friends laughing away in the corner. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, which is exactly why it's so popular. As for why social interaction matters, I'd say it's absolutely essential because, at the end of the day, humans are social creatures. We're simply not built to spend all our time alone. Meeting friends face to face helps us let off steam, share our worries and feel like we belong somewhere. Without that kind of contact, I think people can easily feel isolated and down in the dumps. And that ties in nicely with how friendships shape our happiness. To be honest, having a solid support network makes a huge difference. When something good happens, your friends double the joy, and when things go wrong, they help you get through it. There's a lot of truth in the saying that a problem shared is a problem halved. I suppose, at the end of the day, the friends we surround ourselves with genuinely determine how content and grounded we feel in life.

bulletPoints: Can you describe a place where people often meet friends?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A place where people meet friends:
One of the most prominent meeting spots in my city is a vibrant lakeside park. It features beautifully landscaped gardens, cozy cafes, and expansive walking trails. On weekends, it is consistently packed with groups having picnics and playing sports. The convivial atmosphere makes it the ideal backdrop for friends to catch up and unwind effortlessly.
Why social interaction is important:
Social interaction is fundamentally paramount because humans are inherently social creatures. Establishing connections prevents the debilitating effects of isolation and chronic loneliness. Through mutual conversations, we exchange ideas and gain diverse perspectives, which crucially expands our understanding of the world and acts as a psychological anchor during stressful periods.
How friendships influence happiness:
Friendships profoundly dictate our happiness levels. Having a robust support system ensures that joy is multiplied when shared and sorrrow is divided during hardships. Friends provide a safety net of unquestioning loyalty. A deep connection stimulates dopamine release, proving the ancient wisdom that "a sorrow shared is a sorrow halved."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Do'stlar uchrashadigan joy:
Mening shahrimdagi eng mashhur uchrashuv joylaridan biri bu gavjum ko'l bo'yidagi parkdir. Unda chiroyli obodonlashtirilgan bog'lar, shinam kafelar va keng piyoda yo'laklari mavjud. Dam olish kunlari u piknik qilayotgan va sport o'ynayotgan guruhlar bilan doimiy ravishda to'lib-toshadi. Qulay muhit do'stlarning uchrashishi va bemalol dam olishi uchun ideal sharoit yaratadi.
Ijtimoiy muloqotning ahamiyati:
Ijtimoiy muloqot juda muhim, chunki odamlar tabiatan ijtimoiy mavjudotlardir. Aloqalarni o'rnatish izolyatsiya va surunkali yolg'izlikning halokatli oqibatlarining oldini oladi. O'zaro suhbatlar orqali biz fikr almashamiz va turli nuqtai nazarlarga ega bo'lamiz, bu esa dunyoqarashimizni sezilarli darajada kengaytiradi va stressli davrlarda psixologik tayanch vazifasini o'taydi.
Do'stlikning baxtga ta'siri:
Do'stlik bizning baxt darajamizni chuqur belgilaydi. Kuchli qo'llab-quvvatlash tizimiga ega bo'lish, quvonch ulashilganda ko'payishini va qayg'u qiyinchilik paytida bo'linishini ta'minlaydi. Do'stlar shubhasiz sadoqatning xavfsizlik to'rini ta'minlaydi. Chuqur aloqa dofamin ajralishini rag'batlantiradi, bu esa "qayg'u ulashilsa, yarmi ketadi" degan qadimiy hikmatni isbotlaydi.

questions.prompt: People should live in big cities rather than small towns.
questions.sampleA1: I like city. City is good. More shops.
questions.sampleA2: I think city is better. Because there are more things to do. And more jobs. But small town is quiet.
questions.sampleB1: I think living in a big city is better. For example, there are more opportunities for work and education. Also, there are more things to do like going to the cinema or restaurants. However, it can be more expensive to live in a city. But I still prefer it.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is quite a divisive topic, and honestly I can see the appeal of both sides. On the one hand, those in favour of big cities have a strong case. For a start, cities are where the jobs are — there are far more opportunities when it comes to careers, and the pay tends to be higher too. On top of that, you've got much better access to top-notch healthcare, universities and public transport. And let's not forget the entertainment — there's always something going on, whether it's museums, concerts or restaurants. In short, city life can be really exciting and full of possibilities, and there's rarely a dull moment. On the other hand, though, living in a city isn't all a bed of roses. It can be incredibly crowded and stressful, and the cost of living is often through the roof — rent alone can eat up most of your salary. Small towns, by contrast, offer a much slower, calmer pace of life. People tend to know their neighbours, so there's a real sense of community that you rarely find in the city. You can properly relax and get away from all the noise and pollution. As for my own view, I suppose it really comes down to what stage of life you're at. Personally, while I'm young and ambitious, I'd rather put up with the hustle and bustle of the city for the sake of my career. But further down the line, I can definitely picture myself settling down somewhere quieter.

Shahar markazlarida sanoat va biznesning yuqori darajada jamlanganligi yanada dinamik ish bozorini va martaba o'sishi uchun katta imkoniyatlarni yaratadi. Bundan tashqari, shaharlarda muzeylar va teatrlardan tortib xalqaro oshxonalargacha bo'lgan xilma-xil madaniy takliflar ko'proq bo'ladi. Albatta, kichik shaharlarning ham o'ziga xos jozibasi bor, ayniqsa hayotning sekin sur'ati va kuchliroq jamoatchilik tuyg'usi bilan bog'liq. Ammo imkoniyat va madaniy boylik izlayotganlar uchun shahar odatda yaxshiroq tanlovdir.

vocabulary.title: Q8 - Living in big cities vs small towns
idioms: the rat race - "kalamushlar poygasi (shahardagi tuganmas, toliqtiruvchi raqobatli hayot)"
the hustle and bustle - "shovqin-suron / qaynagan hayot"

sentenceStarters: "The debate between urban living versus settling in small towns is…" - "Katta shahar yoki kichik shaharchalarga yashash o'rtasidagi bahs-munozara…"
"Advocates of metropolitan life firmly point out the…" - "Katta shahar hayoti tarafdorlari … ni qat'iy ta'kidlaydilar."

against: Big cities are often crowded and stressful.
The cost of living is usually higher.
Small towns offer a quieter lifestyle.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The debate between urban living versus settling in small towns is highly nuanced. Advocates of metropolitan life firmly point out the unparalleled economic prospects. Cities serve as major hubs for international corporations, offering abundant job opportunities and career progression. Furthermore, they provide vastly superior public infrastructure, ranging from world-class universities to cutting-edge healthcare facilities. Finally, the cultural vibrancy—museums, theaters, and a diverse culinary scene—ensures a dynamic, exciting lifestyle.
Conversely, proponents of rural life argue that cities are overwhelmingly toxic. The relentless hustle inevitably breeds stress, chronic anxiety, and severe noise pollution. Additionally, the astronomical cost of living and exorbitant housing prices make financial stability difficult. In contrast, small towns offer a profoundly peaceful existence, characterized by tight-knit communities where neighbors actually know one another, allowing people to escape the "rat race."
In conclusion, both environments possess unique merits. The choice ultimately depends entirely on an individual's priorities—whether they crave the ambition of the concrete jungle or the tranquility of the countryside.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shahar hayoti va kichik shaharlarda yashash o'rtasidagi bahs juda nozik masala. Metropolitan hayot tarafdorlari beqiyos iqtisodiy istiqbollarni qat'iy ta'kidlaydilar. Shaharlar xalqaro korporatsiyalar uchun asosiy markaz bo'lib, mo'l-ko'l ish imkoniyatlari va martaba o'sishini taklif qiladi. Bundan tashqari, ular jahon darajasidagi universitetlardan tortib, eng zamonaviy tibbiy muassasalargacha bo'lgan juda yuqori darajadagi davlat infratuzilmasini ta'minlaydi. Nihoyat, madaniy hayotiylik — muzeylar, teatrlar va xilma-xil oshxona sahnasi — dinamik, hayajonli turmush tarzini ta'minlaydi.

Aksincha, qishloq hayoti tarafdorlari shaharlar juda zaharli ekanligini ta'kidlaydilar. Tinchim bilmas harakat doimiy stress, surunkali tashvish va kuchli shovqin ifloslanishini keltirib chiqaradi. Bundan tashqari, osmono'par turmush narxi va haddan tashqari uy-joy narxlari moliyaviy barqarorlikni qiyinlashtiradi. Bunga javoban, kichik shaharlar chuqur tinch hayotni taklif qiladi, bu qo'shnilar bir-birini biladigan, odamlarga "kalamushlar poygasi"dan qochishga imkon beradigan ahil jamoalar bilan ajralib turadi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, har ikki muhit ham o'ziga xos afzalliklarga ega. Tanlov oxir-oqibatda butunlay shaxsning ustuvorliklariga bog'liq — ular beton o'rmonning ambitsiyalarini xohlashadimi yoki qishloqning osoyishtaligini.
